title: Dissection and surgical approaches to the mouse jugular-nodose ganglia
protocol: Weigh the animal.
Administer preoperative analgesia subcutaneously: Buprenorphine (0.05 mg/Kg).
Administer anticholinergics subcutaneously: Atropine (0.1 mg/Kg), 15 minutes before starting surgery.
Place the animal inside an induction chamber with 3% isoflurane for 1 minute.
Maintain isoflurane at 1.5% after transferring the animal to the surgical platform.
Apply ophthalmic ointment to both eyes.
Fix the animal on a supine position using tape.
Spread hair-removal cream from chin to thorax.
Wipe away the hair-removal cream and hair using saline pads five minutes later.
Disinfect the surgical area with povidone-iodine prep pads.
Disinfect the surgical area with 75% ethanol pads, three times.
Use mice that are 6–8 weeks old and weigh between 20–25 g for JNG surgery.
Retract the submandibular glands to expose the carotid sheath.
Reposition the sternocleidomastoid muscle laterally and the omohyoid muscle medially to fully expose the carotid sheath.
Separate the vagus nerve from the carotid artery until the JNG is accessible.
Inject 500 nL of CCK-SAP at a rate of 2 nL/s into the JNG using the Nanofil Sub-Microliter Injection System mounted on a programmable syringe pump.
Slide the spinal hook along the common carotid artery toward the skull base.
Tear the rostral carotid sheath and connective tissue to uncover the vagus trunk and superior laryngeal branch.
Carefully shred down the brown adipose tissue to gain access to the superior cervical ganglion and the root of the hypoglossal nerve.
Push the superior cervical ganglion rostrally to expose the hypoglossal nerve roots and the vagus nerve.
Separate and pull the hypoglossal nerve caudally away from the vagus nerve root with a spinal cord hook.
Cut a midline incision using a scalpel to expose the submandibular glands.
Bilaterally retract the submandibular glands outwards to expose the trachea.
Laterally retract the sternocleidomastoid muscle.
Retract the omohyoid muscle towards the midline to expose the carotid sheath.
Pierce through the carotid sheath and separate the common carotid artery using a spinal cord hook.
Expose the vagus nerve after separating the common carotid artery.
Open the carotid sheath rostrally until fully exposing the vagus root and superior laryngeal branch.
Carefully remove connective tissue surrounding the vagus root to expose the superior cervical ganglion.
Tear off brown adipose tissue located on the ventral side of the superior cervical ganglion to uncover the roots of the hypoglossal nerve and the vagus nerve.
Pull the superior cervical ganglion rostrally to reveal the hypoglossal nerve and the vagus nerve.
Detach the hypoglossal nerve away from the vagus nerve using a spinal cord hook.
Gain a clear view of the JNG swellings, which are located immediately adjacent to the base of the skull where the vagus nerve exits.
Immerse all surgical tools into saline before contacting any carotid arteries or cranial nerves.
Frequently drop saline into the surgical area to maintain it hydrated.
Gently lower and insert the 36G beveled NanoFil needle into the JNG swellings with the micropositioner.
Infuse 200 nL CCK-SAP at 2 nL/s.
Close the skin with a sterile suture and apply povidone-iodine.
Transfer the animal into a clean cage warmed at 37°C.
Apply post-operative analgesia, carprofen, 5 mg/Kg (s.c.) twice/day for three consecutive days.
Dilute Carprofen stock solution (50 mg/mL) with 0.9% saline into working solution (0.5 mg/mL).
Store diluted Carprofen refrigerated and dispose of after 30 days.
Induce deep anesthesia with 3% isoflurane.
Transcardially perfuse 50 mL of saline + heparin solution.
Perfuse 50 mL ice-cold 4% PFA in PBS.
Dissect the skull and cervical tissues.
Wash tissue thoroughly with PBS for 3 h, three times.
Remove excess skin and adipose tissue.
Truncate the cervix between the first and second cervical spinal cord segments.
Cut the skullcap.
Remove the brain and spinal cord.
Expose the upper surface of the skull.
Locate the occipital bone, temporal bone, hypoglossal canal, and jugular foramen.
Cut the occipital bone along the midline.
Push the occipital bone away from the temporal bone to expose the vagus nerve and JNG.
Isolate the vagus nerve and JNG using Vannas spring scissors.
Discriminate the light-colored jugular foramen from the hypoglossal canal.
Split the occipital bone along the midline.
Remove the temporal bone away from the occipital bone.
Expose and dissect the vagus nerve using Vannas spring scissors.
Dissect the jugular foramen nerve group (JNG).
